page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left: only the outer edge of the left page is visible, a strip of cut-off line ends, with no full text block. Right: page 29, one text column of running text, with no margin notes. Below the text: a signature "D 3" and the catchword "quod".

main_text.p: ecclesiam redimere & regenerare, ut cum à reatu, tum à dominio peccati liberetur. Fortis sit ille heros oportet ; qui caput serpentis conteret, omniaque diaboli opera perfringat. Veritas est prædicatum, quod huic Deo forti tribuitur. Vox אֱמֶת[?] veritatem & fidelitatem notat : atque ita dicitur ille, quia illi tuto creditur, qui nunquam sefellit credentium fidem, nec sœdus suum violavit ; sed se constantem atque fidelem exhibuit in præstandis promissis, dum pollicitationes cumulatè exhibuit. Adde quod & veritas audiat propter soliditatem corporis præ umbris ; lex enim umbras tantum rei habebat in placitis ; veritas tantum in populi assertore & vindice spectatur : quasi Præco porrecto in rupem & sponsorem jam factum redemptorem digito designaret objectum fidei eum esse, qui spem patrum & finem umbrarum adducto jam solido piaculo adimpleverat.

Et absque injuria. Vox עוֹל[?] notat proprie factum contra alterius jus, quo quoquam detrahitur, quod eidem debetur ex jure ; atque adeo injuriam ; Lev. 19 : 16. Psal. 7 : 4. 53 : 2. Negatur de Deo. Psal. 92 : 16. Jer. 2 : 5. & de Christo Jes. 53 : 9. Hic præco & patronus causæ rupis, negans eam fecisse cuiquam injuriam, amolitur ab ea accusationem adversariorum, contra eos asserens, quod nullius jura violaverit, nec Dei per blasphemiam, qui sine rapinâ se potuit Deo parem sistere : nec principum aut regum hujus mundi, qui regnum tantum cœleste fundare molitus fuerat : nec populi, quem non seduxit, sed per veram doctrinam ad Deum reducere conatus fuerat.
Justus & rectus est ipse. Justus dicitur, qui ex jure suo sibi partim competenti, partim acquisito agit ; atque ita rupis se operi applicans perfecto, id tentavit, quod

page.notes: The left page survives only as cut-off line ends at the left edge of the scan; those fragments are transcribed as they appear and are not complete words. "opuli" has its first letter cut off, so the [?] marks a likely p. Hebrew words (veritatem and injuria) are read from a small, blurred print; the letters are uncertain and marked [?]. The printed "Jef." is read as "Jes." with long s. The running head is set in spaced capitals. No marginal notes are visible on the right page.
